Answer: E
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates increased opacity in the right upper zone with crowding of the bronchovascular markings, which is a direct sign of volume loss (atelectasis) in the right upper lobe. This finding distinguishes it from hyperlucency (air trapping), middle lobe pathology (which would obscure the right heart border), or tension pneumothorax (which would cause a contralateral mediastinal shift).
